properties.natural_language: After Fusaka activation, the default gas limit configuration value in the EL client MUST be 60,000,000.

reachability.notes: Requires operator misconfiguration or client implementation error in default gas limit value. Not directly exploitable by external attacker.

properties.severity_justification: Configuration default correctness; no direct security impact unless combined with other issues.

properties.natural_language: After the block producer reads the gas limit config, the block header gas limit field MUST equal the configured gas limit value (60M by default post-Fusaka).

reachability.notes: If the block producer incorrectly reads or applies the gas limit, blocks could have wrong capacity. Internal to block production.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect gas limit in block header could cause minor inconsistency but validators would vote to correct it.

properties.natural_language: The total gas used by all transactions in a block MUST NOT exceed the block gas limit field in the block header.

reachability.notes: An attacker could submit transactions or blocks where cumulative gas exceeds the block gas limit. Block validation must enforce this invariant.

properties.severity_justification: Violation of this invariant in block validation could cause consensus splits between nodes that accept and reject over-gas blocks, affecting >33% of network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing a block with gas used > gas limit passes validation.

properties.natural_language: Operator-configured gas limit overrides MUST take precedence over the Fusaka default of 60M.

reachability.notes: Configuration handling, not externally exploitable.

properties.severity_justification: Configuration precedence issue; no direct security impact.

properties.natural_language: A block received via P2P gossip MUST have its serialized size validated to be less than 10 MiB before acceptance into the CL gossip layer.

reachability.notes: An adversarial block builder can construct worst-case blocks via P2P. If block size validation is missing or incorrect, oversized blocks could crash CL nodes or disrupt gossip.

properties.severity_justification: A single oversized block bypassing gossip validation could disrupt block propagation for >33% of the network, causing missed slots.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating a block under 60M gas that exceeds 10 MiB serialized size, or a block that bypasses size validation.

properties.natural_language: For any block with gas limit <= 60,000,000, the worst-case serialized block size MUST be strictly less than 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes).

reachability.notes: If a novel adversarial construction produces blocks > 10 MiB within 60M gas, CL gossip would reject them, causing network splits between EL-validated and CL-rejected views.

properties.severity_justification: If this invariant is violated, an attacker could produce valid EL blocks that CL rejects, causing a full consensus-execution layer split affecting all nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: construct a block within 60M gas whose serialized size >= 10 MiB.

properties.natural_language: After CL gossip validation, a block that exceeds the 10 MiB gossip limit MUST be rejected and NOT propagated to peers.

reachability.notes: A malicious peer could send oversized block messages. If CL does not reject them, the gossip network could be flooded.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to reject oversized blocks could enable gossip layer flooding, affecting >33% of network propagation.

properties.natural_language: A transaction submitted to the mempool MUST have its gas limit validated against the block gas limit (60M post-Fusaka) before acceptance.

reachability.notes: Attacker can submit transactions via P2P with arbitrarily high gas limits.

properties.severity_justification: A transaction exceeding block gas limit accepted into mempool could cause resource exhaustion or inconsistent mempool behavior across >5% of nodes.

properties.natural_language: If a per-transaction gas cap (EIP-7825) is active, the transaction gas limit MUST also be validated against that cap, independent of the block gas limit.

reachability.notes: Without per-tx cap enforcement, a single transaction could consume entire 60M gas block, enabling worst-case execution.

properties.severity_justification: Missing per-tx gas cap check could allow single transactions to monopolize block capacity, causing execution time spikes on >5% of nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Only applicable if EIP-7825 is active in Fusaka.

properties.natural_language: After gas validation, a transaction with gas limit exceeding the per-transaction cap MUST be rejected and NOT included in any block.

reachability.notes: If rejection fails, oversized transactions could enter blocks.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to reject invalid transactions could cause consensus disagreements between nodes enforcing the cap and those not.

properties.natural_language: The gas limit voting mechanism MUST converge toward the default gas limit value (60M) when no operator override is set, regardless of EL client implementation.

reachability.notes: A bug in gas limit voting convergence could prevent the network from reaching the intended 60M target.

properties.severity_justification: Slow convergence affects capacity but not safety directly.

properties.natural_language: Existing smart contracts MUST NOT exhibit changed security properties (e.g., reentrancy feasibility, gas estimation assumptions) solely due to the increased block gas limit from 36M to 60M.

reachability.notes: Attacker could exploit contracts that assume lower block gas limits for reentrancy guards or gas estimation.

properties.severity_justification: Contracts relying on block gas limit assumptions could be exploited, potentially affecting >5% of network value.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires identifying specific contracts affected by the gas limit increase.

properties.natural_language: The raw blob input MUST have exactly BYTES_PER_BLOB bytes before blob-to-polynomial conversion.

reachability.notes: Blob data from Engine API (semi-trusted) or network could have incorrect length. Missing validation could cause buffer overflows or incorrect polynomial encoding.

properties.severity_justification: Invalid blob length bypassing validation could corrupt polynomial encoding, leading to invalid cells distributed to >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Exploitable via compromised EL providing malformed blobs through engine_getBlobsV2.

properties.natural_language: After blob_to_polynomial conversion, the resulting polynomial MUST have exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB evaluation points.

reachability.notes: Internal correctness property; violation indicates implementation bug in polynomial conversion.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect polynomial dimensions would produce invalid cells, potentially causing data availability failures on >5% of the network.

properties.natural_language: After compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs completes, exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB KZG proofs MUST be produced.

reachability.notes: Cell count mismatch would break PeerDAS distribution and verification.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong cell count would cause all peers requesting specific cell indices to fail verification, potentially affecting >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: Each field element in the polynomial MUST be less than BLS_MODULUS throughout the encoding pipeline (blob → polynomial → cells).

reachability.notes: Malformed blob from Engine API could contain bytes that decode to values >= BLS_MODULUS, causing undefined behavior in field arithmetic.

properties.severity_justification: Field element overflow could corrupt KZG proofs, enabling invalid data to pass verification, affecting data availability for >33% of network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: blob data that produces field elements >= BLS_MODULUS.

properties.natural_language: All input arrays to verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (commitments_bytes, cell_indices, cells, proofs_bytes) MUST have equal length.

reachability.notes: Untrusted P2P peer can send mismatched array lengths. Missing check could cause out-of-bounds access.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds memory access from mismatched arrays could crash nodes, taking down >33% of the network with a single crafted message.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: crafted P2P message with mismatched array lengths.

properties.natural_language: Each commitment_bytes MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT bytes, each proof_bytes MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_PROOF bytes, and each cell MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_CELL bytes.

reachability.notes: Malicious peer sends cells/proofs/commitments with incorrect byte lengths.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect byte lengths could cause buffer overreads or deserialization failures, potentially crashing >33% of nodes.

properties.natural_language: Each cell_index MUST be less than CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB to prevent out-of-bounds access to root-of-unity tables.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends cell_index >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB to trigger out-of-bounds access in root-of-unity lookup.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds array access could crash or corrupt node state for >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: P2P message with cell_index >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB.

properties.natural_language: Deserialization of commitment bytes via bytes_to_kzg_commitment() MUST perform BLS G1 subgroup check, rejecting points not on the BLS12-381 curve.

reachability.notes: Missing subgroup checks allow invalid curve points that could break pairing verification soundness.

properties.severity_justification: Missing BLS subgroup checks could allow forged proofs to pass verification, completely breaking data availability guarantees for all nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: crafted commitment bytes not on BLS12-381 G1 subgroup that cause verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch to return true for invalid data.

properties.natural_language: Each field element in cell data MUST be less than BLS_MODULUS when converted via bytes_to_bls_field().

reachability.notes: Attacker sends cell data with field elements >= BLS_MODULUS to cause undefined field arithmetic behavior.

properties.severity_justification: Field element overflow could bypass KZG proof verification, allowing invalid cells to be accepted by >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: cell bytes where a field element >= BLS_MODULUS passes verification.

properties.natural_language: The Fiat-Shamir challenge r MUST be computed deterministically from the exact input (including duplicate commitments) such that any change to any input produces a different challenge.

reachability.notes: If the Fiat-Shamir challenge is not computed correctly over all inputs, an attacker could craft inputs that produce a predictable challenge, enabling proof forgery.

properties.severity_justification: Fiat-Shamir challenge predictability would break batch verification soundness, allowing invalid cells to be accepted across all nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: crafted inputs that exploit Fiat-Shamir weakness to pass invalid batch verification.

properties.natural_language: After successful batch verification (pairing check returns true), every cell in the batch MUST be a correct evaluation of the polynomial committed by its corresponding commitment at the specified coset.

reachability.notes: If the pairing check has implementation bugs, invalid cells could pass verification.

properties.severity_justification: Broken pairing verification completely undermines data availability, allowing invalid data to be considered available by all nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: cells with incorrect evaluations that pass batch verification.

properties.natural_language: Recovery inputs MUST satisfy: len(cell_indices) == len(cells), count >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2, no duplicate indices, ascending order, all indices < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, each cell length == BYTES_PER_CELL.

reachability.notes: Cells collected from P2P peers may be adversarially chosen. Missing recovery input validation could cause incorrect polynomial reconstruction.

properties.severity_justification: Invalid recovery inputs could produce incorrect reconstructed data, causing data availability inconsistencies for >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: Cell indices provided for recovery MUST be in strictly ascending order with no duplicates.

reachability.notes: Duplicate or unordered indices from P2P could cause vanishing polynomial construction to fail or produce incorrect results.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect recovery due to duplicate indices could cause inconsistent data availability on >5% of nodes.

properties.natural_language: After successful recovery, the reconstructed polynomial's first FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB coefficients MUST exactly match the original polynomial that produced the input cells.

reachability.notes: Implementation bug in Reed-Solomon recovery could silently produce incorrect polynomial.

properties.severity_justification: Silent data corruption in recovery would mean nodes have different views of blob data, breaking data availability for all nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: specific cell set that causes recovery to produce incorrect polynomial.

properties.natural_language: After recovery, the recomputed cells and proofs MUST match what would be produced by compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs on the original blob.

reachability.notes: If recomputed cells don't match the original, recovered data distributed to peers would fail their verification.

properties.severity_justification: Mismatched recovered cells distributed to peers would cause verification failures, disrupting data availability for >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: The polynomial multiplication in recovery MUST satisfy len(a) + len(b) - 1 <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB for all inputs.

reachability.notes: An adversarially chosen set of missing cells could maximize the vanishing polynomial degree. If the assertion fails, it could crash the node.

properties.severity_justification: Assertion failure during recovery could crash nodes attempting to recover data, affecting >5% of the network.

properties.natural_language: Raw bytes received from a network peer MUST undergo byte length validation for commitments (BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT), proofs (BYTES_PER_PROOF), and cells (BYTES_PER_CELL) before any deserialization.

reachability.notes: Primary trust boundary for PeerDAS. Any malicious peer can send arbitrary bytes.

properties.severity_justification: Missing byte length validation is the first line of defense against malformed P2P data. Bypass could crash >33% of nodes.

properties.natural_language: All cell_indices received from an untrusted peer MUST be validated to be < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB before use as array indices.

reachability.notes: Out-of-bounds cell index from P2P peer can trigger array index out-of-bounds in root-of-unity lookups.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds access could crash or corrupt node, affecting >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: BLS group element deserialization (bytes_to_kzg_commitment, bytes_to_kzg_proof) MUST perform subgroup checks to ensure points are on the BLS12-381 G1 curve.

reachability.notes: Missing subgroup checks allow points from the cofactor group, breaking pairing verification soundness.

properties.severity_justification: Missing subgroup checks break KZG proof soundness, allowing invalid data to be accepted as available by all nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: G1 point not in prime-order subgroup that causes valid pairing result for invalid data.

properties.natural_language: Each field element decoded via bytes_to_bls_field() MUST be validated to be < BLS_MODULUS, rejecting values that would wrap around.

reachability.notes: Values >= BLS_MODULUS in cell data could cause incorrect field arithmetic, potentially allowing forged proofs.

properties.severity_justification: Field element overflow in cryptographic operations could break proof verification for >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: After all validation and deserialization steps complete successfully, the resulting elements MUST be safe for use in cryptographic operations (pairing checks, polynomial arithmetic) without further validation.

reachability.notes: This is a trust transition property: once elements pass all checks, they are trusted internally.

properties.severity_justification: Architectural completeness property ensuring the validation pipeline is sufficient.

properties.natural_language: The Fiat-Shamir challenge hash MUST be computed over the original input commitments (including any duplicates), not the deduplicated set.

reachability.notes: Inconsistency between implementations on whether to hash original or deduplicated commitments could cause verification disagreements.

properties.severity_justification: Cross-client disagreement on Fiat-Shamir input could cause consensus split between >33% of nodes running different implementations.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing different implementations compute different challenges for same input.

properties.natural_language: PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY MUST be a valid generator of the multiplicative subgroup of the required order in the BLS12-381 scalar field.

reachability.notes: Constant correctness; if PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is wrong, all FFT operations are incorrect.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong root of unity would break all cell encoding and verification across all nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC: show PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY is not a generator of the correct subgroup.

properties.natural_language: Fork transition MUST be atomic: the system is either fully operating under pre-Pectra rules or fully under post-Pectra rules, never a mix.

reachability.notes: Non-atomic fork transition could leave nodes in inconsistent state, causing consensus splits.

properties.severity_justification: Non-atomic fork transition could cause network-wide consensus split affecting all nodes.

properties.natural_language: Pectra fork activation MUST only occur when current_epoch >= PECTRA_ACTIVATION_EPOCH (364032 for mainnet).

reachability.notes: Off-by-one in epoch comparison could cause premature or delayed fork activation.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect fork activation timing would split nodes between pre/post fork rules, affecting all nodes.

properties.natural_language: Prague (EL) and Electra (CL) MUST activate at the same slot/block boundary.

reachability.notes: EL/CL activation mismatch would cause Engine API disagreements and potential network split.

properties.severity_justification: EL/CL fork activation mismatch would split the entire network.

properties.natural_language: After Prague fork activation, all 4 core EL EIPs (EIP-2537, EIP-2935, EIP-7623, EIP-7702) MUST be simultaneously active.

reachability.notes: Partial EIP activation would cause inconsistent behavior between clients.

properties.severity_justification: Partial EIP activation in some clients would cause consensus disagreements affecting >33% of the network.

properties.natural_language: After Electra fork activation, all 6 core CL EIPs (EIP-6110, EIP-7002, EIP-7251, EIP-7549, EIP-7685, EIP-7691) MUST be simultaneously active.

reachability.notes: Partial CL EIP activation would cause attestation/block validation disagreements.

properties.severity_justification: Partial CL EIP activation would cause consensus splits affecting >33% of validators.

properties.natural_language: Nodes that have not implemented EIP-7642 (optional networking upgrade) MUST remain able to participate in consensus and not be partitioned from the network.

reachability.notes: If EIP-7642 becomes de facto required despite being optional, nodes without it could be partitioned.

properties.severity_justification: Network partition of nodes without optional EIP could affect >5% of the network.

properties.natural_language: The combined activation of 11 EIPs MUST NOT introduce cross-EIP interaction bugs that would not be present when each EIP is activated independently.

reachability.notes: Cross-EIP interactions (e.g., EIP-7702 + EIP-7623 calldata cost changes) could create unexpected behavior not caught in isolated testing.

properties.severity_justification: Cross-EIP bugs could create exploitable conditions affecting >33% of the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating specific cross-EIP interaction bug.
